item.title: Microsoft says services fully restored after global outage
item.description:
Microsoft was a source of frustration for computer users when it stopped working on Nov. 12, 2026. AP Photo/Michel Euler The Microsoft services outage that began on Nov. 12, 2026, is not like other internet outages. The failure affected the Microsoft 365 suite of productivity services, including the video conferencing and collaboration platform Teams, AI assistant Copilot and, significantly, the Outlook email service. Microsoft reported on Nov. 13 that the company is “continuing to see improvements in service availability” but that “some users may still experience intermittent access issues or delayed email delivery.” Despite decades of predictions about its decline , email remains a central pillar of how organizations function. Password resets, invoices, legal notices and cybersecurity incident response coordination all depend on it. The Microsoft 365 outage affected businesses,…

item.title: Israel Used a U.S.-Made Missile to Kill Six at Gaza’s Nasser Hospital
item.description:
Throughout Israel’s war on Palestine, doctors Thaer Ahmad and Feroze Sidhwa spent months at Nasser Hospital in the southern Gaza city of Khan Younis, where they provided care as volunteers and survived a raid and an airstrike on the complex. On Wednesday evening, they were in an Uber in New York headed to a screening of their film about their time in Gaza when they realized Nasser was the target of another Israeli airstrike. “They just hit Nasser again,” Ahmad said, turning from the front seat toward Sidhwa. “I think Rizk is dead.” He was referring to Dr. Rizk Abu Shaaira, an experienced surgeon and fixture of the Palestinian medical community whom both had worked alongside at the hospital and who appears in their film “ American Doctor .” When Israel attacked Nasser Hospital on Wednesday — for at least the seventh time since the genocide escalated in 2023 — Abu Shaaira was one of the…

item.title: Hungary: Millions in hidden cash found in Orban graft probe
item.description:
Anti-corruption agency carried out searches as part of investigation into Orbán-era minister accused of taking bribes Hungary’s anti-corruption agency said on Friday it had seized cash worth $19.5m (£14.8m) buried in forests and hidden elsewhere while investigating an ex-minister of nationalist former leader Viktor Orbán’s cabinet. Miklós Seszták, Hungary’s minister of national development between 2014 and 2018, is accused of taking bribes in a scheme involving the state transport company, purchasing secondhand buses at inflated prices. item.title: Democrats fumbled the Hegseth impeachment. That could be a blessing in disguise | Claire Finkelstein
item.description:
Most of America bemoans political gridlock in the nation’s capital. DC area commuters deplore the city’s transit gridlock. But Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth may now be a fan of DC’s legendary traffic snarls. It appears that crosstown traffic may have prevented him from becoming only the third Cabinet secretary ever impeached by the House of Representatives. The House voted 211-204 this week to divert an effort by Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) to impeach Hegseth. House Republicans moved to block a straight, up-or-down vote on impeachment. Instead, Republicans forced a vote on sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee. That’s where they’d go to die. If the House failed to sidetrack the articles, Members would have then voted on actual impeachment.
